title: Identity and postal address
goal: Collect the employee's name, date of birth and complete home address once, so HR can post documents and the pension fund can identify the employee.
context: HR posts many documents to employees, so it needs a complete, normal postal address, as written on an envelope (F-TR-009, F-TR-010). The pension fund needs first name, last name and date of birth to register the employee (F-SC-002 to F-SC-005, F-SC-015). The country of the home address is also the employee's country of residence. Source tax uses it to decide whether the employee lives in Switzerland (F-TR-034, F-TR-037). Every later step depends on this answer, so this feature comes first.

stories.title: Provide name and date of birth for pension registration
stories.i_want: every new employee's first name, last name and date of birth
stories.so_that: I can register the employee for occupational pension, which I cannot do while any of these is missing
stories.priority_reason: The pension fund marks all three as required and rejects a registration without them ('<Field> is required.'), so missing values block the registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Name is always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their first name and last name; both are required for every employee and cannot be left empty; both are passed on to the pension fund for the registration

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their date of birth as a date in the form DD.MM.YYYY; it is required for every employee and cannot be left empty; it is passed on to the pension fund for the registration

acceptance_criteria.title: Missing identity data is pointed out before submitting
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has left their first name, last name or date of birth empty
acceptance_criteria.when: they try to complete the identity step
acceptance_criteria.then: they are told which of these is missing and cannot complete the step until each is provided, so that no registration reaches the pension fund with these required values missing

stories.title: Provide a complete postal address
stories.i_want: every new employee's full home address: street, house number, postcode, town and country
stories.so_that: I can post documents to the employee without missing parts of the address
stories.priority_reason: HR posts many documents to employees and states the address must be complete; an incomplete address blocks HR's regular postal process.

acceptance_criteria.title: All address parts are always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for street, house number, postcode, town and country of their home address; every part is required for every employee and none can be left empty; the address is passed on to HR

acceptance_criteria.title: Address is a normal postal address
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee enters their home address
acceptance_criteria.then: only the parts of a normal postal address, as written on an envelope, are asked (street, house number, postcode, town, country) with no extra address parts; the country is given by its English name (e.g. Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein)

acceptance_criteria.title: Address is asked once and works for addresses abroad
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee lives inside or outside Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the same address questions apply in both cases, and the address is asked only once in the whole onboarding

stories.title: Use the home address country as country of residence
stories.i_want: the country of the employee's home address to be used as their country of residence, without asking for residence separately
stories.so_that: it is known whether the employee lives in Switzerland, which decides whether they are subject to source tax and which further questions apply
stories.priority_reason: Employees living abroad are always subject to source tax; without this answer source tax cannot be determined and later steps cannot decide what to ask.

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence is not asked separately
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: onboarding needs to know where the employee lives
acceptance_criteria.then: the country of the home address is used as the country of residence and the employee is not asked a separate question about where they live

acceptance_criteria.title: Living abroad means subject to source tax, whatever the nationality
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee's home address is outside Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is subject to source tax regardless of nationality, and the nationality question used only for residents of Switzerland is not asked; if the home address is in Switzerland, nationality is asked so that liability can be decided by the later steps

acceptance_criteria.title: Address comes first
acceptance_criteria.then: identity and home address are asked before any question whose need depends on where the employee lives
